lab.title: Laboratory analysis
lab.summary: Make measurements that other people can trust. A laboratory worker prepares samples, uses a method consistently and records enough detail for someone else to interpret the result.
tasks: Prepare and label samples so their identity is preserved.
Run comparisons or reference samples to check the method.
Record results, units and limitations before sharing findings.
lab.collaborators: Scientists, process engineers and quality teams
lab.classroom_connection: A repeatable method and a fair comparison matter as much as a single impressive number.

process.title: Process engineering
process.summary: Turn a useful transformation into a workable sequence of equipment and operating steps. Process engineers consider what enters, what leaves and what conditions the system must maintain.
tasks: Draw a flow of materials and energy through the system.
Compare operating conditions and equipment options.
Use trial results to revise the process and communicate constraints.
process.collaborators: Laboratory staff, operators, mechanical designers and controls specialists
process.classroom_connection: Conservation of matter and energy connects classroom calculations to process decisions.

food.title: Ingredient and formulation science
food.summary: Investigate how ingredients behave in a product. This work connects a material’s composition to properties such as texture, stability or performance in a mixture.
tasks: Choose a property to compare across formulations.
Prepare controlled trials and observe changes over time.
Explain the trade-offs between ingredients and processing conditions.
food.collaborators: Biochemists, laboratory technicians and product-development teams
food.classroom_connection: Molecules and mixtures help explain why two ingredients can behave differently.

instrument.title: Instrument development and testing
instrument.summary: Help build and check the equipment that produces measurements. Instrument work joins hardware, software and experiments rather than treating a reading as automatically correct.
tasks: Check performance using a known reference.
Investigate drift, noise or inconsistent readings.
Document tests so later users know what the instrument can establish.
instrument.collaborators: Scientists, electronics specialists and software developers
instrument.classroom_connection: Measurement uncertainty is part of using a tool responsibly.

applications.title: Scientific applications
applications.summary: Connect an instrument to the question a user needs to answer. Applications work involves selecting a method, interpreting results and explaining limitations.
tasks: Choose a measurement approach for the sample.
Compare outputs with reference information.
Explain what further tests would resolve ambiguity.
applications.collaborators: Laboratory users, instrument engineers and researchers
applications.classroom_connection: A pattern is evidence to interpret, not a label that proves an answer by itself.

mechanical.title: Mechanical design and prototyping
mechanical.summary: Translate a need into a component or machine that can be built and tested. Designers use dimensions, material properties and constraints to evaluate alternatives.
tasks: Create and revise drawings or a digital model.
Choose materials and dimensions for the intended conditions.
Compare the prototype with its requirements and refine the design.
mechanical.collaborators: Machinists, fabricators, test staff and customers
mechanical.classroom_connection: Geometry, forces and material properties shape real design trade-offs.

machining.title: Machining and dimensional inspection
machining.summary: Make parts fit their intended purpose by controlling dimensions. Machining combines tools, setup and measurement; finishing a part is not the same as proving it meets its specification.
tasks: Interpret a drawing and plan a sequence of cuts.
Set up the machine and check the workpiece.
Measure critical dimensions and document deviations.
machining.collaborators: Designers, production teams and quality inspectors
machining.classroom_connection: Tolerance describes an acceptable range rather than a perfectly exact number.

controls.title: Instrumentation and controls
controls.summary: Keep a process measurable and responsive. Controls work connects sensors, decisions and actuators so the system can respond when conditions change.
tasks: Check whether sensors are reading reliably.
Compare measurements with the intended operating range.
Test how the system responds to a change or fault.
controls.classroom_connection: Feedback uses a measured result to inform the next action.

maintenance.title: Aircraft maintenance
maintenance.summary: Investigate condition, carry out authorized maintenance and preserve the records behind a decision. Aircraft maintenance work relies on approved procedures and appropriate qualifications.
tasks: Inspect a component using the applicable procedure.
Compare findings with documented limits and escalate uncertainty.
Record work and test results for the maintenance decision.
maintenance.collaborators: Licensed AMEs, avionics specialists, engineering and quality teams
maintenance.classroom_connection: A visual impression alone is not enough evidence that a part is safe.

avionics.title: Avionics and electronics
avionics.summary: Work on the electronic systems that allow aircraft to communicate, navigate and collect data. Troubleshooting means distinguishing a faulty sensor from wiring, power or software problems.
tasks: Trace a signal through connected components.
Use test equipment to compare expected and measured behaviour.
Document the fault and verify the result after authorized work.
avionics.collaborators: Aircraft maintenance teams, electrical designers and software developers
avionics.classroom_connection: Circuits and signals become useful when the complete system works reliably.

quality.title: Quality and traceability
quality.summary: Make it possible to explain how a result or product was produced. Quality work checks records, methods and acceptance criteria so variation can be investigated rather than hidden.
tasks: Check that materials and samples have traceable identities.
Compare recorded results with defined acceptance criteria.
Investigate deviations and document what changed.
quality.collaborators: Production, laboratory, engineering and customer teams
quality.classroom_connection: Repeated results need both measurements and records of the conditions that produced them.

bioprocess.title: Bioprocess development
bioprocess.summary: Develop repeatable ways to make and purify biological materials. This work connects molecular science to manufacturing conditions and checks whether a change improves the process.
tasks: Define a comparison between process conditions.
Track production and purification steps for each batch.
Use analytical results to decide which change to test next.
bioprocess.collaborators: Molecular scientists, analytical staff and quality teams
bioprocess.classroom_connection: Knowing a sequence or molecule is different from producing a reliable batch of it.

drone.title: Drone operations
drone.summary: Plan and carry out flights for a specific task while coordinating with the people responsible for the site. The aircraft is one tool within an operational plan.
tasks: Review the task, site and operating constraints.
Check the aircraft and coordinate the flight with relevant personnel.
Record observations and equipment issues after the flight.
drone.collaborators: Site operations, wildlife specialists and data analysts
drone.classroom_connection: Flight performance must be considered alongside the task and the surrounding environment.

wildlife.title: Wildlife monitoring and interpretation
wildlife.summary: Observe how animals respond to an intervention and ask whether the change lasts. This work needs consistent observations and attention to other causes of changing behaviour.
tasks: Define how bird activity will be counted.
Compare observations before and after an intervention.
Record weather, season and other factors that could explain a difference.
wildlife.collaborators: Drone operators, airport staff and environmental teams
wildlife.classroom_connection: Behavioural response is evidence; reduced sightings alone do not prove a lasting safety outcome.

spatial.title: Spatial data and mapping
spatial.summary: Turn measurements tied to places into usable spatial information. The work involves coordinates, scale and checking that datasets describe the same location and time.
tasks: Check coordinate systems and measurement dates.
Align and inspect spatial datasets.
Present maps or models with their limitations.
spatial.collaborators: Surveyors, engineers, field operators and software teams
spatial.classroom_connection: Models can be detailed while still containing gaps or misaligned measurements.

geoscience.title: Geoscience and interpretation
geoscience.summary: Explain what rock measurements suggest about geology. Geoscientists combine observations with context and use additional tests where a scan leaves uncertainty.
tasks: Describe core and identify changes along it.
Compare sensor patterns with geological observations or assays.
Communicate alternative interpretations and uncertainty.
geoscience.collaborators: Core technicians, data scientists and exploration teams
geoscience.classroom_connection: A measurement of a sample is not automatically a measurement of the whole deposit.

software.title: Software and data systems
software.summary: Build the tools that move, process and display information. Reliable software needs testing against missing, delayed and unexpected data as well as ideal examples.
tasks: Translate a user need into a testable behaviour.
Build and test a data-processing or display feature.
Investigate failures and document assumptions about inputs.
software.collaborators: Domain experts, designers, users and hardware teams
software.classroom_connection: An algorithm’s output depends on the quality and meaning of its inputs.

millwright.title: Industrial machinery assembly and maintenance
millwright.summary: Make machinery work together as a physical system. Millwright work connects assembly, alignment, inspection and troubleshooting.
tasks: Read equipment drawings and plan assembly steps.
Align and connect mechanical components.
Check operation and record problems that need adjustment.
millwright.collaborators: Designers, operators, electricians and fabrication teams
millwright.classroom_connection: Small alignment errors can change how forces and motion pass through a machine.

fabrication.title: Metal fabrication and welding
fabrication.summary: Join and assemble material into usable structures. Fabrication work follows drawings and procedures, then checks whether the finished work meets its requirements.
tasks: Read dimensions and prepare components.
Use the specified joining process and sequence.
Inspect the assembly and communicate any deviation.
fabrication.classroom_connection: Material properties and heat affect the result of a joining process.

materials.title: Materials research and testing
materials.summary: Investigate whether a material improves a product for a defined purpose. A useful comparison separates the effect of the added material from other changes in the test.
tasks: Prepare comparable samples with and without an additive.
Measure a relevant property under consistent conditions.
Explain performance changes alongside uncertainty and practical constraints.
materials.collaborators: Chemists, process engineers and product developers
materials.classroom_connection: Stronger, lighter and more conductive are different properties requiring different tests.

power.title: Power-electronics design
power.summary: Control how electrical energy moves between components. Power-electronics work combines circuit design with testing, thermal limits and the behaviour of the complete system.
tasks: Choose and document a circuit design.
Test its response across operating conditions.
Investigate losses and component limits before revising the design.
power.collaborators: Electrical technologists, firmware developers and manufacturing teams
power.classroom_connection: Power describes the rate of energy transfer; stored energy describes how much is available.

weather.title: Weather-data interpretation
weather.summary: Use observations to understand changing atmospheric conditions. Weather-data work checks where and when a measurement was made before combining it with other evidence.
tasks: Check the position, time and quality of observations.
Compare measurements across altitude or time.
Identify gaps and explain how they limit an interpretation.
weather.collaborators: Meteorologists, instrument teams and data engineers
weather.classroom_connection: More measurements can help, but uneven coverage can still leave important gaps.
